question: Where does live tiny-manifest latency accumulate: transport/proxy/auth/database versus payload?
limitations: Development-machine HTTP requests are not browser paint or p95. Two samples per path are diagnostic only.
No production configuration or business data mutations. GET routes can perform existing incidental IP tracking.
Remote RPC timings include Supabase HTTP gateway and network, not only PostgreSQL execution.
No Server-Timing instrumentation exists in deployed library route; exact handler/auth/RPC attribution needs instrumentation.

local_claim_verification.note: Diagnostic use of installed SDK with genuine owned QA ES256 token. Does not change deployed authentication. Cached JWKS verifies signature and expiry; account/session revocation semantics need explicit review before replacing live getUser.

vercel.evidence: x-vercel-id in this file: Frankfurt ingress, US East function execution

render.evidence: Root agent observed Render service Settings Region textbox in authenticated dashboard during this diagnosis

supabase.evidence: Previously observed Session pooler aws-1-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com for production project

deployment_geography.consequence: Browser in Europe -> Vercel function US East -> Render Oregon -> Supabase Ireland; serial authorization and RPC calls repeat long-distance backend/database round trips.

findings.statement: Warm direct backend guest 520.9 ms versus dev proxy 540.9 ms; warm authenticated backend 1051.6 ms versus dev proxy 1053.5 ms. These separate samples do not provide an exact causal subtraction.

Manifest response is 3813 bytes for 6 guest books and 4486–4487 bytes for 7 QA books. After response headers, receiving the whole body took 0.2–11.2 ms. Payload transfer does not explain second-scale latency.

Warm direct Supabase manifest HTTP RPC is 126–131 ms from this European machine, including network and gateway. Root subsequently measured the same production SQL function through a read-only EXPLAIN transaction: first guest execution 97.600 ms; following authenticated QA execution 6.544 ms. These are two differently scoped calls, not a cold/warm series or p95.
Direct Supabase auth getUser is 101.7–140.2 ms from this machine. ES256 cached SDK getClaims verifies the owned QA token in 0.86–0.89 ms after a 257.78 ms first JWKS request.
The catalog handler serially awaits remote getUser and then one compact manifest SQL RPC.
Legacy track-ip middleware is blocking despite an obsolete fire-and-forget comment: at first (token, IP) and every 5 minutes it awaits user resolution plus profiles upsert before route dispatch.
Blocklist reload adds an awaited Supabase SELECT at cold process/cache expiry (60 seconds). It is not awaited again for each warm request.

Initial page middleware awaits remote Supabase getUser before HTML; API routes are excluded. After hydration the controller resolves local session, settles own writes/reading activity, reads cache, then fetches the manifest. Profile status does not gate the index once user identity is known.

Earlier 2503 ms result measured browser navigation through observed title DOM, not an isolated index request and not PostgreSQL execution. It includes document loading/hydration/automation observation overhead.

recommendations.action: Co-locate Render backend with Supabase in Europe; keep old Oregon service and DB unchanged for rollback during candidate validation. Set dev Vercel function region near backend/DB. Measure equivalent warm/cold routes before domain cutover.
recommendations.reason: Eliminates cross-ocean serial backend/auth/DB round trips; main observed infrastructure mismatch. Moving only the Vercel proxy is insufficient, as warm direct backend is already slow.

recommendations.action: Add request stage timings for middleware, auth, manifest RPC, total handler and proxy, plus browser navigation-to-request/request-to-index timestamps. Keep payload/order/no-cache behavior unchanged.
recommendations.reason: Provides exact attribution and acceptance evidence rather than inferring PostgreSQL speed from small JSON size.

recommendations.action: Remove duplicate blocking IP telemetry work from the manifest critical path by reusing validated request identity and deferring captured-client metadata writes with a lifecycle-safe mechanism.
recommendations.reason: Preserves telemetry while avoiding repeated auth and writes before the index response.

recommendations.action: Evaluate cached JWKS getClaims for ES256 bearer validation in v2 after explicitly covering revoked/disabled/deleted user and issuer/audience/scope behavior; retain strict invalid-bearer rejection.
recommendations.reason: Warm local verification measured under 1 ms; this is a proposed auth behavior change, not part of the current deployment.

stop_condition: HTTP budget completed: 15/15 bounded read-only HTTP calls by this agent. Root subsequently supplied a separate production read-only EXPLAIN; no additional application API measurements or source/production changes by this agent. Before/after region comparison remains a proposed experiment.

postgresql_explain_followup.mode: Root-reported read-only transaction; saved output contains BEGIN, SET, EXPLAIN ANALYZE and ROLLBACK
limitations: These two executions differ in scope and cache/planning state; they do not isolate a cold/warm difference or establish a distribution.
Execution time excludes the HTTP auth check, PostgREST, Render/Vercel transport, browser startup and paint.
Detailed SQL inputs/provenance are owned by root; this agent inspected the saved EXPLAIN output, not reran the query.
